newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel falls against dollar in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel falls against dollar in dull trade.

text.p: The Israeli shekel was fixed lower against the dollar on Monday in dull trading as the market continued to seek direction, dealers said.
"Trading was very thin today. There are no sellers or buyers. With a very small sum you can move the market either way," said a dealer at the First International Bank of Israel.
"Trading is still very nervous and spreads are very high at 100-150 points. In the next few days the shekel is expected to stabilise at 3.55 to 3.57 shekels per dollar," the dealer said.
He added that he expected the market to remain volatile for some time to come. "The truth is that nobody knows where this market is going."
The dealer said the appointment of Yaacov Neeman as finance minister had no impact on trading.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu named Neeman to the finance portfolio on Monday morning. National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon, distrusted by the market, had been the leading candidate for the post.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5690 shekels against 3.5530 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8786 against 3.8591 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.1761 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.1399 on Friday, and against the mark at 2.0440 shekels compared with 2.0053 on Friday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5670 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
